transcript.content: Hello. I'm a psychiatrist here to help you today. What brings you in to see me?
I'm here because I have an overwhelming and intense fear of enclosed spaces and elevators. It has become really difficult for me to manage, so I decided I needed to seek some help.
Is your intense anxiety mostly limited to enclosed spaces and elevators, or do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different areas of your everyday life?

My anxiety is strictly limited to enclosed spaces and elevators. I don't experience constant or generalized worry about other areas of my daily life. It is really just those specific situations that trigger this intense fear.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of enclosed spaces and elevators?
I've been dealing with this intense fear for about one year and eleven months now. It has been almost two years of constantly struggling with these situations.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms are characterized by an intense, situational fear of enclosed spaces and elevators (claustrophobia) that has lasted for nearly two years (well over the 6-month DSM-5 requirement). The anxiety is strictly confined to these specific situations and does not generalize to other areas of life, ruling out Generalized Anxiety Disorder. The presentation fully satisfies the criteria for Specific Phobia, and no other differential diagnoses are indicated.
